messages:
maria: heads-up: after the mkdocs-material upgrade, our linkcheck started flagging a number of fragment targets as 404. seems like slug rules changed.
docsite-ci: linkcheck failures: /guides/migration#default-params (404), /api/embeddings#usage (404), /tutorials/sdk#cpp-example (404)
sam: oh great. did the slugifier drop punctuation this time? parentheses and plus signs are disappearing from ids?
lee: yep. mkdocs-plugin-anchors + the new slugify removes non-alphanum. previously we kept certain chars so old links break.
maria: short-term we can add explicit header ids to the affected headings: e.g. `### Default params {#default-params}`. longer-term we should backfill programmatically.
julian: agree. i suggest a script that scans markdown for headings and for any inbound references to missing anchors, insert an explicit id matching the old-style anchor if possible. keeps history stable.
alexa: curious edgecase: headings like "C++ API examples" previously mapped to "c++-api-examples" but new slug is "c-api-examples". we need a mapping table for ++ -> plus-plus or explicit ids.
sam: can we also avoid touching use_directory_urls? that option caused other redirects to break in another repo.
maria: proposed script (dry-run mode included):
```
# tools/backfill_ids.py
import re,sys,os

OLD_SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9\-]")

def legacy_slug(h):
    s=h.lower()
    s=re.sub(r"\s+","-",s)
    s=OLD_SLUG_RE.sub("",s)
    return s

for root,dirs,files in os.walk('docs'):
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith('.md'): continue
        p=os.path.join(root,f)
        txt=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
        def repl(m):
            level=m.group(1)
            title=m.group(2).strip()
            slug=legacy_slug(title)
            if '{#' in m.group(0):
                return m.group(0)
            return f"{level}{title} {{#{slug}}}"
        new= re.sub(r'^(#{2,6})\s+(.+)$', repl, txt, flags=re.M)
        if new!=txt:
            open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(new)
            print('patched',p)
```

lee: nice. run in dry-run first, commit only the needed files. also add a unit test in linkcheck that maps known legacy anchors to the new explicit ids so future slugifier changes show up in CI.
julian: i'll draft a small migration note for CONTRIBUTING and add an example table: "C++ -> {#c-plus-plus-api}" suggestion.
docsite-ci: scheduled re-run in 8m :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
maria: opened PR with the script + a handful of manual id fixes + migration note: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/503 please review.
sam: quick review: the legacy_slug regex strips plus signs; for cases like C++ we should special-case /\+\+/ -> plus-plus before stripping. i'll push a tiny commit.
alexa: i patched one md that had `# Query (SQL)` -> `{#query-sql}` explicitly. that fixed the /guides/migration#query-conventions link.
docsite-ci: linkcheck complete. remaining fail: /api/embeddings#usage (404)
lee: embeddings page had the Usage heading under a H4 inside a callout; the regex only handled ##-######. updated script to pick up deeper headings too.
maria: reran script, committed patch. running linkcheck again.
docsite-ci: linkcheck OK :tada:
sam: great. can we add a tiny check in pre-commit to detect headings without explicit ids when the repo has a legacy-link mapping file?
julian: yes, add docs/migration/legacy-anchors.md with a short table and a note for contributors.
maria: done, changelog note added. closing thread.
